name: Yoga / Surya Namaskar for height

lead: Some height programmes and forum threads promote yoga stretches and Surya Namaskar (Sun Salutation), a flowing sequence of about twelve linked postures, as a way to stand taller. The payoff people want is a lengthened, decompressed spine and better posture.

Proponents say the stretching lengthens the spine and improves posture, a route to a small change in standing height. Published studies of Sun Salutation measure energy use (about 2.9 to 7.4 METs) and muscle activation, and none was found measuring height.

paras: People do the sequence or a stretching routine regularly, often in the morning, and combine it with other posture and height habits. Results people look for are better posture and a more upright stance over weeks of practice.
Yoga is generally an ordinary physical activity with the usual strain risks. No height-specific harms are documented.

angle.text: Yoga and Surya Namaskar are used as stretching routines to lengthen the spine and improve posture so you stand a little taller. Research on yoga covers fitness and flexibility rather than height.

lead: Yoga and Surya Namaskar (Sun Salutation) are marketed in some height-increase programmes and forum threads as stretching routines that can add height. Surya Namaskar is a flowing sequence of about twelve linked yoga postures associated with Hindu devotion to the sun god Surya.[1]

The Sun Salutation's history is uncertain; no hatha yoga text recorded the sequence before the 19th century, and it was popularised in the early 20th century, including through a 1928 publication by the Rajah of Aundh and the teaching of Krishnamacharya.[1] Published research on it concerns energy expenditure and muscle activation, such as an energy cost ranging from about 2.9 to 7.4 METs, rather than height outcomes.[1]
No studies were found testing yoga or Surya Namaskar as a way to increase height.

paras: Height-focused programmes typically present stretching poses, spinal extensions and the Sun Salutation sequence as methods to lengthen the spine and body. Variations differ by yoga school, including Iyengar, Sivananda and Ashtanga.[1]

A 2014 study measured muscle activity during Ashtanga sequences and found different muscle use in beginners and instructors, and a 2016 systematic review placed the energy cost of Sun Salutation from light to vigorous depending on style.[1] These studies did not measure height.

lore.intro: Yoga for height appears mainly in marketing and in height-gain forum threads as a gentle, low-cost routine.

claims.claim: Surya Namaskar and stretching poses can make you taller

timeline.event: The Rajah of Aundh publishes a text popularising and naming the Sun Salutation.[1]
Vishnudevananda's illustrated yoga book presents the sequence as fitness exercise.[1]
